description: YuNet face detector from OpenCV Zoo. THE SELECTED DETECTOR: chosen over SCRFD because its weights are permissively licensed, and issue #3 leaves SCRFD's pretrained weights unusable for anything but development.

pad_value.source: opencv/opencv modules/objdetect/src/face_detect.cpp, FaceDetectorYNImpl::padWithDivisor: copyMakeBorder(..., BORDER_CONSTANT, 0) -- the runtime every published YuNet number is measured through. Agreed by the training repository: ShiqiYu/libfacedetection.train yunet_train/tasks/face/transforms.py::build_eval_transforms uses Pad(size=(image_size,image_size), pad_value=0) followed by Normalize(mean=0, std=1), and the size_divisor variant uses pad_value=0 too. Because this config has scale 1 with empty mean and std, pixel 0 and tensor 0.0 coincide, so the two spaces agree here as well.

batching.verified_against: Codex, issue #31: onnxruntime.InferenceSession on the upstream face_detection_yunet_2023mar.onnx reports input 'input' with shape [1,3,640,640], and a batch of 2 fails dimension validation with 'index 0: Got 2 Expected 1' (ONNX Runtime 1.28, macOS arm64). Corroborated from the upstream export tooling, which needs no checkpoint to read: in ShiqiYu/libfacedetection.train, yunet_train/cli/export_onnx.py declares --dynamic-export as store_true (default OFF) and yunet_train/engine/onnx_export.py::parse_input_shape hardcodes the leading dimension to 1, so the published export is static unless someone asked for otherwise. NOT RE-MEASURED IN THIS CHANGE: the checkpoint is a git-LFS object and was not downloaded here.

license.training_data: WIDER FACE. Its terms are separate from the model's and need their own check.
license.note: Desk assessment: OpenCV Zoo publishes YuNet under MIT for both code and weights, which is why it is the selected detector rather than SCRFD. NOT VERIFIED at source -- a human must read the current licence and set verified/verified_at before this can be promoted past candidate.

eval.note: No benchmark has been run. YuNet is expected to trail SCRFD on small faces, which is the case that matters in group photos. The cost lands as recall, not precision: a missed face is absent from an album, while the precision-first threshold and review queue keep a wrong face out. Quantifying the gap is the first eval-harness job.

notes:
SCORE RULE: confidence is sqrt(clamp(cls,0,1) * clamp(obj,0,1)) -- the clamped GEOMETRIC MEAN of the separate classification and objectness heads, which is why both appear in outputs. It is declared as the `geometric_mean_score` step so a registry-driven host can apply it without hardcoding anything per model id. An earlier version of this file said the product, and at score_threshold 0.6 the product discards roughly 84% of the detections YuNet accepts -- which reads as a weak detector rather than a bug. Confirmed against opencv/modules/objdetect/src/face_detect.cpp.

DECODER: not SCRFD's distance-to-four-sides. Boxes are centre-offset plus exponentiated size; landmarks are cell-relative and linear.

NMS: OpenCV rounds each box to an integer cv::Rect2i BEFORE cv::dnn::NMSBoxes, so IoU is computed on integer rectangles and its width/height convention differs from a float box by one pixel. Declared as `integer_rect_nms` rather than plain `nms` because the two disagree on boxes sitting near the IoU threshold -- and a disagreement there means one face becomes two, or two adjacent faces in a group photo become one.

THRESHOLDS: 0.6 and 0.3 are the OpenCV Zoo defaults, starting points rather than tuned values; re-tune against our own benchmark libraries before promotion.

COORDINATES: decoded against the letterboxed 640x640 input, and must be un-letterboxed before being normalised against the ORIENTED image for FaceRecord.

SHAPES AND BATCHING CORRECTED AGAINST THE REAL GRAPH (issue #31). The declared output shapes were rank-2 [-1, C]; the checkpoint emits rank-3 [1, N, C] with N fixed per stride (6400/1600/400 at 640x640, matching 80x80/40x40/20x20 grids with one anchor per location -- unlike SCRFD's two). Batching claimed supported/max 8/dynamic; the graph's input is a static [1, 3, 640, 640], so batch is 1 and the input size is not negotiable either. WHY UPSTREAM NEVER NOTICED: OpenCV consumes YuNet through cv::dnn, which reshapes a fully-convolutional network to whatever it is given, so upstream needs no dynamic axis and the published export does not have one -- corroborated in the export tooling, where libfacedetection.train's export_onnx.py declares --dynamic-export as store_true (default off) and onnx_export.py::parse_input_shape hardcodes the leading dimension to 1. Under ONNX Runtime the declared shape is binding. The failure was never silent at the tensor level -- ORT raises -- but the CONFIG was silent, and execution.py clamping requests to the session's real leading dimension (PR #25) is what let the wrong claim keep passing review.

PADDING (issue #33): pinned to pixel 0. Three upstream sources agree (OpenCV's FaceDetectorYN, and both eval-transform paths in the training repository), and this config's identity normalisation makes pixel space and tensor space the same number, so there is nothing left to disagree about.

TWO NUANCES RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. First, upstream does not letterbox at all: cv::dnn reshapes the network to the image's own size and pads only to the next multiple of 32. We letterbox to a square because the ONNX graph's input is fixed at 640x640 (issue #31), so our padded band is much larger than any band the model was evaluated with. Second, YuNet's TRAINING augmentation fills out-of-image crop regions with 128, not 0 -- transforms.py::_crop_image_with_padding -- so the network has seen both. 0 is pinned because it is what the letterbox band specifically is upstream, in both eval and deployment; 128 belongs to a different operation.
